Usage: LinkServer.exe flash [OPTIONS] DEVICE COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Flash operations. On multi-core targets, the functionality is available only
  on the primary core.

  DEVICE can be:
  - <DEVICE_NAME>:<BOARD> pair, same as `devices --filter` parameter
          - ':<BOARD>' alone selects the board's default device
          - '<DEVICE_NAME>:' selects the device paired with a board (instead of the standalone device)
  - device configuration file with extension `.json`.
          Use `config` command for generating such a file from an existing device
  - 'auto' : Auto-select the device using the probe's target identification information

COMMAND:
  blank        Check that the specified flash region is blank
  dump         Dump the flash region specified by ADDR and SIZE to a...
  erase        Erase all flash
  erase-range  Erase all flash sectors overlapping the range specified by...
  load         Program the flash with the given FILE arguments
  resurrect    Attempt to unlock the device by running masserase-script
  verify       Verify that the flash contents match the given FILE...

ARGS for a specific command are shown when using --help with the respective
subcommand

OPTIONS:
  -p, --probe TEXT                Probe serial/index to use. If it starts with
                                  # then it is interpreted as a probe index,
                                  otherwise it is interpreted as a probe
                                  serial substring. Unnecessary if only one
                                  probe is connected. Note: if the
                                  terminal/shell interprets # as a beginning
                                  of a comment, put the probe index under
                                  quotes. Example: `--probe '#1'`.
  -u, --update-mode [none|check|auto|forced]
                                  MCU-Link firmware update MODE for the
                                  selected probe (applies to MCU-Link probes
                                  only). Supported modes: `check` : checks if
                                  a firmware update is possible; `auto` :
                                  updates the firmware only if the version
                                  running on the probe is older than the local
                                  one; `forced` : always updates the firmware
                                  [default: check]
  -t, --update-timeout INTEGER    Timeout value in seconds needed to allow the
                                  OS to detect MCU-Link probes rebooting
                                  during firmware update.  [default: 5;
                                  1<=x<=60]
  -o, --override <POINTER>=<VALUE>
                                  Override device's JSON configuration.
                                  <POINTER> is a JSON pointer to the property
                                  that needs to be modified. <VALUE> should be
                                  a valid JSON value, otherwise it is
                                  interpreted as a string. Example: `-o
                                  /device/memory/2/flash-
                                  driver=LPC553x_S.cfx`. If <VALUE> is not
                                  given, the property that <POINTER> points to
                                  is deleted. Can be used multiple times.
  --bootconfig <data>             Controls target boot configuration by
                                  driving the MCU-Link ISP_CTRL pins during
                                  resets. This option is aimed to be used for
                                  board designs with on-board MCU-Link probe
                                  (running firmware version 3.108 or later).
                                  <data> is a 4 characters string describing
                                  how each ISP_CTRL[3..0] pin should be
                                  handled: '0' (= drive low), '1' (= drive
                                  high), 'x' (= do not drive). Use 'xxxx' to
                                  turn off / cancel a previous bootconfig
                                  option.   In addition, <data> can be a boot
                                  configuration friendly name from device's
                                  JSON configuration, if available
                                  ('bootconfigs' settings).
  -B, --no-boot                   Do not boot probes (applies to LPC-Link/LPC-
                                  Link2 only)
  -I, --boot-image [bridged|non-bridged|vcom-serial]
                                  LPC-Link 2 boot type. Bridged LPC-Link2
                                  probes include the USB to SPI/UART bridge
                                  functionality; non-bridged includes only
                                  debug and VCOM functionality.  [default:
                                  bridged]
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
